feature: Shift M and Command Shift M jump between markers
summary: On a video, Shift M puts the playhead on the next marker and Command Shift M on the one before, as in Premiere. Sequence carries both rows with their keys, dimmed when there is no marker that way.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: shift-m-jumps-between-markers-walk, go-to-marker-menu-rows-walk.

try.do: Open a recording. Without clicking anything, press M at three different moments while you scrub.
Press Shift M three times: the playhead lands on each marker in turn.
Press Shift M once more: at the last marker nothing moves, and the canvas tool stays as it was.
Press Command Shift M until it stops on the first marker.
Open Sequence in the menu bar: Go to Next Marker and Go to Previous Marker sit under Add Marker's group, dimmed when there is nowhere to go.
Open a still picture and press Shift M: it still cycles the selection tools, as in Photoshop.

evaluate: Do the two keys land where your hands expect after Premiere?
Should Command Shift M also work after you click the canvas, as it does now, or only while the timeline has the keyboard like Shift M?
Does a press at the last marker doing nothing feel right, or would you want a small cue?
Would you also want Go to Next and Previous Marker on the ruler's right-click menu?
rough: No mock covers marker navigation or the Sequence menu's rows; the keys and the menu rows follow Premiere.

Shift M only means Next Marker while the timeline has the keyboard (the ring round the dock). After a click on the picture it goes back to cycling the selection tools, the same rule as M, I and O. Command Shift M has no other meaning, so it works either way.
The ruler's right-click menu does not carry the two rows: every row there acts at the moment you clicked, and a jump from the playhead would be the one row that does not.
